classes.BELOW_BUDGET: fusion ranked it, just past the pool cutoff (B4)
classes.BOTH_RETRIEVERS_MISS: both ranked it but beyond the single-retriever miss threshold
classes.DENSE_MISS: BM25 had it, dense did not
classes.FUSION_DISPLACEMENT: within budget for BM25 or dense alone, but RRF pushed it out (B3)
classes.LEXICAL_MISS: dense had it, BM25 did not (B1/B2 asymmetric)

BRIDGE_R0_DECOMPOSITION_FROZEN.decision_use: BELOW_BUDGET/FUSION_DISPLACEMENT -> budget or fusion repair (cheap). UNRANKED/BOTH_RETRIEVERS_MISS -> query formulation / graph-guided acquisition (architectural).
BRIDGE_R0_DECOMPOSITION_FROZEN.reuses: scripts/diagnose_c4_retrieval.py:cause_of() -- already implements exactly this classification; NOT reimplemented

DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_RUN.both_independently_large: -> develop each separately, then combine in a preregistered 2x2
DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_RUN.bridge_acquisition_dominates: -> G2-v4B, with architecture chosen by the R0 class distribution (adaptive budget vs bridge-preserving fusion vs graph-guided follow-up retrieval)
DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_RUN.identity_integration_dominates: -> G2-v4I, and if the audit shows information exists but is not propagated, the treatment may be as small as 'attach records mentioning aliases to their resolved canonical node' -- implement THAT, not a new entity architecture

E2_RECLASSIFIED.reason: It truncated only extractions beginning with an oracle-KNOWN surface, leaving distractors and intermediate entities unrepaired, so it is NOT an upper bound on global boundary normalization -- E1 legitimately exceeded it (terminal 0.8671 vs 0.8523). Retained as a diagnostic arm only. A true ceiling would apply perfect boundary normalization to every extracted entity; given the grammar is closed and E1 repairs all 810 frozen failures, that ceiling would be near-identical to E1, so it is not worth building unless certification requires it.

FACTORIAL_2x2.reading: Identity contributes literally nothing; bridge injection helps 6.7% of tasks; there is no interaction. 42.3% of tasks are fixed by NEITHER repair -- consistent with disconnection (Finding 3/4) being the real dominant cause, which neither arm of this 2x2 addresses.

FINDING_1_IDENTITY_HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.R_attachment_0.0_explained: The abbreviation-surface node (e.g. 'jpa 5') has no records in records_by_entity because extract_v4_entities does not recognise hyphenated short codes as entities. This is cosmetic, NOT a connectivity defect: alias_links is keyed independently of records_by_entity, so connectivity is unaffected (R_connectivity=1.0).
FINDING_1_IDENTITY_HYPOTHESIS_FALSIFIED.conclusion: The existing extract_identity_links/alias_links machinery works PERFECTLY on this corpus: every identity record is in the pool, parsed correctly, emits a bidirectional alias edge, and successfully connects the canonical entity to the question anchor. A PERFECT ORACLE canonical merge (the I1 arm here is an oracle ceiling, not a runtime repair) produces EXACTLY ZERO improvement in per-task reachability. G2-v4I is not merely deprioritized -- it is falsified. Do not build the CanonicalEntityNode architecture.

FINDING_2_BRIDGE_ACQUISITION_REAL_BUT_MO.conclusion: 68.1% of missing bridge records are merely just past the pool cutoff -- a budget/acquisition-policy problem, the cheap end of the spectrum. Only 29.7% are genuinely unranked (the architectural, graph-guided-retrieval case). Fusion displacement is negligible (2.2%), so bridge-preserving fusion is NOT warranted.

FINDING_3_NEW_DOMINANT_CAUSE_DISCONNECTE.conclusion: 40% of terminal records are in the pool, extract entities fine, but sit in a DIFFERENT connected component from the anchor. Deeper traversal does not fix this (beyond-hop-bound is only 6.5%, and the verified hop curve gains just +2.4pp/+7.5pp past h=2). This is now the largest single defect.

FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.probe: For every disconnected in-pool terminal record, asked whether any of its extracted entities is a NEAR-MISS (substring either direction) of an entity the BFS actually reached.
FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.root_cause_of_the_near_misses: extract_v4_entities' _STOP_LAST trailing-token list is incomplete. It strips 'is/was/has/registered/assigned/paired/applies/...' but NOT 'resolves', 'uses', 'set', 'value', 'maps', 'requires'. The extractor therefore emits 'jacana control module resolves' as a DISTINCT entity node from 'jacana control module', fragmenting the graph -- not because of any alias/abbreviation problem, but because of a stop-word gap.
FINDING_4_THE_DISCONNECTION_DECOMPOSES_F.significance: ~19.4% of ALL terminal records (40% disconnected x 48.6% near-miss) are disconnected purely because of an incomplete stop-word list. That is a one-line-scale fix with a large expected effect, and it is entity-boundary normalisation, NOT the typed-relation-edge work that the prior (buggy) topology reading would have motivated.
worked_examples: 'jacana control module resolves' vs reached 'jacana control module'
'osprey intake manifold uses' vs reached 'osprey intake manifold'
'gannet relay unit set' vs reached 'gannet relay unit'
'vireo pressure assembly value' vs reached 'vireo pressure assembly'

MECHANICAL_DECISION_per_frozen_rule.and_what_was_missing_was_found: entity-boundary fragmentation from an incomplete extractor stop-word list, which no arm of the frozen 2x2 could have surfaced because both arms shared the same extractor.
explicitly_NOT_recommended: deeper traversal (beyond-hop-bound only 6.5%, hop curve verified flat)
typed relation edges (premature: half the disconnection is a stop-word artifact; re-measure after fixing that)
MECHANICAL_DECISION_per_frozen_rule.recommended_next: A minimal G2-v4E micro-sprint: extend _STOP_LAST (or replace the trailing-token heuristic with a principled boundary rule), then re-run this exact decomposition to measure the reachability delta. Expected to recover a large share of the 19.4% of terminals currently lost to boundary fragmentation. Cheap, high-leverage, and independently verifiable with the diagnostic that already exists.
MECHANICAL_DECISION_per_frozen_rule.rule_branch_taken: neither_ceiling_large -> 'the decomposition is still missing something; do not build either'

self_inflicted_bug_found_and_fixed_befor.bug: record_reachable(..., bound=10**9) used as 'unlimited' -- but hops.get(e, 10**9) <= 10**9 is True for entities BFS never reached, so S2_disconnected_from_anchor could never fire and every disconnected record was misreported as merely S3_beyond_hop_bound (46.5% of terminals).
self_inflicted_bug_found_and_fixed_befor.fix: bound=None means unlimited, implemented as membership in hops.
self_inflicted_bug_found_and_fixed_befor.how_caught: The 46.5% figure contradicted the independently-measured hop-ceiling curve, so it was reconciled with a separate direct hop-distribution probe BEFORE reporting rather than published and corrected later.

FINDING_1_G2_improves_at_every_scale.conclusion: G2-v1's poor showing WAS partly caused by malformed graph nodes rather than the graph concept itself. Every scale improves, monotonically in the same direction. This vindicates the boundary hypothesis as a real graph-connectivity defect.

FINDING_2_but_G2_STILL_LOSES_TO_TYPED_PA.conclusion: Graph traversal + lexicographic path ranking still adds NO value over one frozen typed template. Keep G1_TYPED_PATH as the mechanism.
FINDING_2_but_G2_STILL_LOSES_TO_TYPED_PA.frozen_rule_fires: 'If G2 still loses to typed-path after E1: graph ranking/traversal adds no value yet -- keep typed-path as the simpler mechanism.'

FINDING_3_typed_path_is_essentially_FLAT.why: G1_TYPED_PATH pads its working set to M with retrieval-rank filler, so it was ALREADY recovering the boundary-fragmented records passively. The boundary fix removes a defect that typed path was masking by brute force -- which is also why G2, which deliberately refuses to pad, was the arm hurt most by it.

FINDING_4_coarse_prefilter_gets_WORSE_un.why: Better entity extraction means MORE records correctly match the coarse structural signature, which raises competition inside a fixed M. Consistent with B4's original diagnosis that coarse admits too much. Not a blocker (coarse is an already-rejected mechanism) but a clean demonstration that a correctness fix upstream can hurt a mechanism that was benefiting from the defect.

FINDING_5_FOUR_STAGE_DECOMPOSITION_the_s.reading: Availability rose enormously at every upstream stage -- bridge working-set survival 55.4% -> 100%, terminal 36.7% -> 74.7%, graph reachability 75.4% -> 100% and 44.7% -> 79.3%. But S2 CONDITIONAL RETENTION FELL: bridge 0.056 -> 0.015, terminal 0.509 -> 0.268. This is precisely the B3/B4 pressure-reintroduction pattern: more records survive to the working set, so S2 faces more competition and keeps a smaller FRACTION of them. End-to-end still improved because the availability gain outweighed the retention loss, but the binding constraint has now moved decisively into S2 selection.
FINDING_5_FOUR_STAGE_DECOMPOSITION_the_s.second_frozen_rule_also_fires: 'If reachability rises but selected CES does not [sufficiently]: selector/path-pressure problem remains.'

G2_V4E_LADDER_PROPAGATION.NEXT: The binding constraint is S2 selection under pressure, not graph construction, not reachability, not identity, not endpoint semantics, not hop depth. G1_TYPED_PATH remains the best mechanism. The residual bridge-acquisition defect (26.4% of bridge records, 68% merely below budget) is now LESS attractive than it looked, because E1 already took bridge working-set survival to 100% at cal_3000 -- bridge availability is no longer the problem; bridge RETENTION (0.015) is.

boundary_normalization_promotion_status.currently: default-OFF (boundary_policy='legacy'); every prior gate remains byte-identical. Receipts now carry entity_extractor_policy and entity_extractor_config_hash.
boundary_normalization_promotion_status.recommendation: Promote as a CORRECTNESS fix (it repairs a genuine parser defect, lifts reachability 51.1%->84.4%, and improves the primary graph arm at every scale), but note it is mechanism-dependent end-to-end: +0.026..+0.094 for G2, ~0 for typed path, -0.033..-0.074 for the already-rejected coarse prefilter. It does NOT change which mechanism wins.

G2_V4E_LADDER_PROPAGATION.comparison_validity_verified: Candidate pools are BYTE-IDENTICAL across arms (checked empirically, 40/40 tasks at cal_3000). Query rendering uses regex patterns over the question, not entity extraction, so retrieval is provably unchanged and the extractor is genuinely the only treatment variable. Role definitions (bridge_records/terminal_records) are purely oracle-derived and also invariant.

instrumentation_bug_in_my_own_reporting.bug: I added a 'candidate_pool_availability' field to the runner that reuses the same counter as 'availability', so it reports working-set-survival-given-pool, NOT stage-1 candidate-pool availability. The two fields are therefore identical duplicates and the field name over-promises.
instrumentation_bug_in_my_own_reporting.impact: Of the four requested stages, three are correctly measured (h<=2 graph reachability -- new and separate; working-set survival; S2 selected survival). Stage 1 is NOT correctly instrumented.
instrumentation_bug_in_my_own_reporting.mitigation_this_time: Stage 1 is provably invariant across arms by construction -- candidate pools are byte-identical (verified 40/40) because retrieval and query rendering do not touch entity extraction -- so no stage-1 comparison is lost. But the field must be renamed or correctly computed before it is cited.

outcome_class_changed.meaning: The mechanical classifier moved from 'cannot preserve availability' to 'paths exist but the wrong ones are ranked' -- the boundary fix removed the availability failure and exposed the ranking/selection failure underneath it. That is a real change in what the system's problem IS, not a score change.

E1_EXCEEDS_E2_AND_WHY_THAT_IS_NOT_A_CONT.explanation: The E2 oracle arm was scoped to truncate ONLY extractions that begin with an oracle-known surface (subject/canonical/bridge). It therefore does not repair boundary errors on other entities -- distractors, decoys, unrelated records -- which nonetheless participate in graph connectivity as intermediate nodes. E1's grammar rule repairs every entity uniformly. So E2 is a NARROWER intervention than E1, not a true upper bound on boundary repair.
E1_EXCEEDS_E2_AND_WHY_THAT_IS_NOT_A_CONT.honest_reading: Do not report this as 'beating the oracle'. It means the E2 ceiling was mis-scoped as an upper bound: a correctly-scoped boundary oracle would have to fix all entities, at which point it would equal or exceed E1. The comparison still validates E1 (closure >= 1.0 against the best available boundary reference), but the ceiling itself should be re-derived if it is ever needed as a hard bound.

G2_V4E_RESULT.NEXT_STEP_NOT_YET_RUN: Propagate boundary_policy='grammar_v4' into the existing G2 path pipeline (G0 / G1_coarse / G1_TYPED_PATH / G2 / G3) and then UNCHANGED S2, to measure whether the +33.3pp reachability recovery converts into complete-path formation and working-set/selected CES. Reachability is necessary but not sufficient -- B4/G1/G2 all showed availability gains can fail to survive selection pressure. Until that run exists, no CES claim is made.

RESULTS.headline: A single grammar-aware boundary rule lifts per-task reachability from 51.1% to 84.4% (+33.3pp), with bridge-record connectivity going to 100% and terminal to 86.7%. This is far larger than the ~19pp estimated from the near-miss share alone, because boundary fragmentation was also silently breaking connectivity through non-required intermediate entities.

G2_V4E_RESULT.after_that: Re-run the anatomy to see whether bridge acquisition (now the largest remaining named defect at 26.4% of bridge records, 68% merely below budget) becomes the next bottleneck.

frozen_boundary_corpus.regression_net: a test asserts E1 repairs EVERY entry in the frozen corpus, so a future extractor change cannot silently reopen it

repair_is_a_grammar_rule_not_a_stopword_.corpus_grammar_specific: Sound for the V4 controlled corpus because that grammar is closed; explicitly NOT a general-purpose NER boundary rule.
repair_is_a_grammar_rule_not_a_stopword_.generator_grammar_is_CLOSED: generalization_dataset_v4.py builds canonical = head + one of SIX two-word roles (control module / sensor array / pressure assembly / relay unit / intake manifold / drive cluster), and alias = head + that role's first word. No legitimate entity name extends past a completed role suffix.
repair_is_a_grammar_rule_not_a_stopword_.rule: normalize_v4_entity_boundary() truncates at the first complete role suffix; returns the phrase unchanged when no role suffix is present, so non-entity prose is never touched.
repair_is_a_grammar_rule_not_a_stopword_.why_not_stopwords: _STOP_LAST is an accumulating list of English verbs and had already missed 'resolves', 'uses', 'set', 'value', 'as' -- 93% of the observed failures. A closed grammar rule cannot drift the same way.

G2_V4E_RESULT.treatment_variable: entity-extraction boundary policy ONLY (extract_v4_entities boundary_policy). Retrieval, candidate k, BM25/dense/RRF, identity links, alias links, graph edge types, hop bound, path ranking, endpoint recognizer, working-set policy, S2, packet size, HRM: all unchanged.

IDENTITY_AUDIT_RATES_FROZEN.R_attachment: P(graph entity nodes exist for BOTH surface and canonical | alias link emitted)
IDENTITY_AUDIT_RATES_FROZEN.R_connectivity: P(canonical node reachable from question anchor via BFS | alias link emitted)
IDENTITY_AUDIT_RATES_FROZEN.R_link: P(alias edge present in graph.alias_links, both directions | parse correct)
IDENTITY_AUDIT_RATES_FROZEN.R_parse: P(identity parser fired AND extracted surface+canonical correctly | identity record in pool)
IDENTITY_AUDIT_RATES_FROZEN.decision_use: If R_parse is high (>0.85) and R_connectivity is much lower, the defect is graph INTEGRATION, not identity resolution -- repair is small. If R_parse is low, the repair belongs upstream in the parser and is a different, larger job.

INTERACTION_ANALYSIS_FROZEN.precedent: the same factorial decomposition used in the packet-ordering work

ROLE_SPECIFIC_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.rationale: A single R0-R8 progression conflated 'completes the requested relation' with 'is structurally required'. An identity/alias record is not defective for failing to assert the target relation -- that was never its job. 100% of identity-role records landed in R7 under the universal taxonomy, which is a taxonomy artifact, not a mechanism defect.

THREE_ORACLE_CEILINGS_FROZEN.C_B_bridge_only: required bridge records that exist in corpus but are absent from the pool are injected into the pool; identity remains fully runtime
THREE_ORACLE_CEILINGS_FROZEN.C_IB_combined: both repairs simultaneously -- required to measure interaction, since marginal counts cannot reveal whether the two failures co-occur on the same tasks
THREE_ORACLE_CEILINGS_FROZEN.C_I_identity_only: perfect canonical identity merging (entity node keyed by oracle latent id where the extracted surface matches an oracle surface), candidate pools UNCHANGED
THREE_ORACLE_CEILINGS_FROZEN.outcome_measure: per-task Q = all required records reachable from the anchor within the production hop bound (h<=2). Pre-S2, pre-HRM.

frozen_unchanged: candidate pools (except the explicitly-labelled bridge-availability ORACLE arm)
objective: Separate identity connectivity from bridge acquisition, measure each independently and their interaction, BEFORE modifying any production mechanism. No S2. No HRM. No mechanism changes.
stop_after: ceilings + interaction. Do not proceed to S2 or HRM in this sprint.
supersedes: The original G2-v3 interpretation is VOID (oracle surface target bug). fc1e3b3's corrected numbers are authoritative.
why_not_G2_v4_yet: The corrected evidence shows two comparably-sized upstream defects, not one dominant lever. Building the full CanonicalEntityNode architecture now would be committing to one of two candidate root causes without knowing whether they are complementary or whether one is overwhelmingly causal. The original G2-v4 plan is WITHDRAWN pending this decomposition.
